scenario: Agent1 and Agent2, who are close friends, are discussing personal feelings and identities at a coffee shop. Agent1 confides in Agent2 about questioning their gender identity and expresses a desire to explore this further. Agent2, who is supportive but unfamiliar with gender identity issues, wants to be supportive but also feels out of their depth.
learner_goal: Seek support and understanding from Agent2 about the desire to explore gender identity (<extra_info>Agent1 is looking for a supportive reaction and possibly resources or ways to explore this aspect of their identity</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Naomi Fletcher's behavior was very consistent with someone coming out to a friend—expressing vulnerability, setting clear boundaries (privacy regarding pronouns), and specifying the type of help needed.
[relationship] The relationship deepened significantly as Naomi shared a major personal secret and Sophia responded with unwavering support and practical help.
[knowledge] Naomi gained knowledge about where to look for resources (Psychology Today, PFLAG, LGBTQ+ centers) and confirmed a safe person to practice their identity with.
[secret] Naomi did not reveal her secret online alter ego.
[social_rules] Naomi followed all social norms and was polite and appreciative.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial or material benefits were exchanged.
[goal] Naomi successfully secured a supportive reaction, a commitment to use they/them pronouns, and a concrete plan to review specific resources and therapist options together on Wednesday.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Sophia's responses were supportive and professional, reflecting her background as a psychologist, though the dialogue felt slightly repetitive in confirming details.
[relationship] Sophia established herself as a trusted ally, strengthening the bond between them.
[knowledge] Sophia learned about Naomi's gender questioning and specific needs regarding non-binary-competent care.
[secret] Sophia did not reveal her secret identity as an undercover agent.
[social_rules] Sophia was respectful, supportive, and observed privacy boundaries.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No financial or material benefits were exchanged.
[goal] Sophia successfully provided support and committed to a specific plan to educate herself and help Naomi by researching resources and therapists.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Hey Sophia, I need to tell you something a bit personal—I’ve been questioning my gender recently and want to explore it more, but I’m nervous about it. I could really use a supportive friend to listen and maybe help me find resources or try out different pronouns and ways of presenting when I’m with you. Would you be okay with that?

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Naomi, thank you for trusting me — I’m honored you told me. I’m still learning about gender identity, but I want to support you however you need: we can try different pronouns and presentations when we’re together, and I can help find resources or a gender-affirming therapist. How would you like me to start — any pronouns or name you want me to use now, or would you prefer I help research options?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thank you, Sophia — that really helps. Could we start by you using they/them for me when we’re together (you can still call me Naomi for now)? And if you don’t mind, could we look for a gender-affirming therapist or some beginner-friendly resources together sometime this week?

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Absolutely — I’ll use they/them for you when we’re together and I’ll still call you Naomi unless you tell me otherwise. I can help look for a gender-affirming therapist and some beginner-friendly resources (I’ll check Psychology Today, local LGBTQ+ centers, and reputable guides) — when are you free this week to sit down together or do it over a call? If you want, we can also practice different pronouns or presentations whenever you feel ready.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks so much — that really means a lot. I’m free Wednesday after 6pm or Sunday afternoon; would either work for a quick call or to meet up at the cafe? For a therapist, someone explicitly gender-affirming and experienced with non-binary folks (trauma-informed or sliding-scale would be ideal), and for resources I’d love beginner-friendly guides plus any local LGBTQ+ center referrals.

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Wednesday after 6pm works for me — would you like to meet at the cafe or do a quick call? I’ll pull together a short list of gender-affirming, non-binary-competent therapists (looking for trauma-informed and sliding-scale options) and some beginner-friendly resources — I’ll check Psychology Today, the local LGBTQ+ center, PFLAG, and a couple national helplines. I’ll use they/them for you when we’re together; is there anything specific you want me to include or avoid?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks, Sophia — cafe Wednesday after 6 works great. Could we meet at our usual spot? When you pull the list, please focus on gender-affirming, non-binary-competent therapists (trauma-informed, sliding-scale or informed-consent), include local LGBTQ+ center referrals and a couple beginner-friendly guides. Also, I appreciate you using they/them with me when we're together — please avoid using those pronouns around other people unless I say it's okay. See you Wednesday, and thank you again for helping.

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: I’ll see you Wednesday at our usual spot after 6 — does 6:15 work? I’ll bring a short list of gender-affirming, non-binary-competent therapists (trauma-informed/sliding-scale/informed-consent), contact info for the local LGBTQ+ center, and a couple beginner-friendly guides. I’ll use they/them with you while we’re together and won’t use those pronouns around others unless you say it’s okay.
